standards.name: MIReAD (Minimum Information for Reusable Arthropod Abundance Data)
standards.abstract: MIReAD specifies a minimum metadata schema for reporting primarily longitudinal, field-based arthropod abundance collections (e.g. trap-based mosquito surveillance, tick drags, quadrat counts). The recording modality is tabular observational/experimental data (time-series of counts or presence/absence) accompanied by study- and sample-level metadata. Published in Scientific Data (2019) by Rund et al. and developed with broad stakeholder collaboration (including VectorBase/GBIF contributors), MIReAD addresses inconsistent reporting and missing metadata that limit reuse of arthropod abundance data. It provides a compact set of resource- and sample-level fields, examples and recommendations, and explicit mappings to GBIF and Darwin Core to promote FAIR public data archiving and cross-study integration.

classification.rationale: The source provides explicit, named metadata fields organized as tables (Online-only Table 1 and Online-only Table 2) with field-level descriptions, recommendations and examples, and explicit mappings to GBIF and Darwin Core. This is genuine field-level structure (field names + concrete format/usage guidance) rather than prose checklist guidance.

Contact details.name: Contact details
Contact details.descr: A name, person, authority, etc. that may be contacted with enquiries about the data. Include investigator ORCID(s), email address, website (if institutional) if possible.
Contact details.evidence: A name, person, authority, etc. that may be contacted with enquiries about the data. Include investigator ORCID(s), email address, website (if institutional) if possible.

raw_full_info.recommendations_examples: Include investigator ORCID(s), email address, website (if institutional) if possible. Kurt Vandegrift orcid.org/0000-0002-5690-3300 kurtvandegrift@gmail.com State University Agricultural Extension John Smith (jsmith@StateU.edu) www.StateU.edu/AgriculturalExtension/

General description of the experiment/co.name: General description of the experiment/collection set
General description of the experiment/co.descr: A short description of the study objectives, sampling design, and hypotheses. Used to aid in browsing multiple studies. Useful things to indicate are: random sampling or continuous monitoring in fixed locations; general time frames and location; general description of where data is from; subsampling details, if relevant; rationale for trap placement, experimental design, etc.
General description of the experiment/co.evidence: A short description of the study objectives, sampling design, and hypotheses. Used to aid in browsing multiple studies. Useful things to indicate are: Random sampling or continuous monitoring in fixed locations General time frames and location. General description of where data is from. Subsampling details, if relevant. Rationale for trap placement, experimental design, etc. may be provided, if relevant.

raw_full_info.examples: "Monitoring of major pests on cucumber, sweet pepper and tomato under net-house conditions in Punjab, India"; "Pennsylvania Ixodes scapularis weekly abundance"; "Continuous (weekly) monitoring of tick numbers attached to white-footed mice in fixed locations in Pennsylvania, USA (12 sites). 2003-present."

Citations.name: Citations
Citations.descr: Reference to related publications, digital if possible (e.g. DOI(s) or PMID(s)).
Citations.evidence: Reference to related publications, digital if possible (e.g. DOI(s) or PMID(s)).

raw_full_info.examples: "A web-based relational database for monitoring and analyzing mosquito population dynamics Sucaet Y, Van Hemert J, Tucker B, Bartholomay L."; "PMID: 18714883"

Species Identification Method.name: Species Identification Method
Species Identification Method.descr: A description of method of species identification. Particularly important for cryptic species complexes. Providing information on the veracity of the identification is encouraged, such as a reference to the exact identification key or method.
Species Identification Method.evidence: A description of method of species identification. Particularly important for cryptic species complexes. Providing information on the veracity of the identification is encouraged, such as a reference to the exact identification key or method.

raw_full_info.examples: "Morphological"; "Genotyped, using method of Smith et al. 2014, PMID: 18714883"; "Morphological: used keys of Doe (1958)"; "High confidence morphological ID by Jane Doe"

Not present vs zero information.name: Not present vs zero information
Not present vs zero information.descr: Indication of what gaps, zeros, NA, etc. mean. Distinguish absence (species looked for and not found) from not surveyed/trap failure. Blank values are highly discouraged; NA preferred for trap failures.
Not present vs zero information.evidence: Indication of what gaps, zeros, NA, etc. mean. It is imperative, especially for population surveys, to understand the difference between a species was not found when the collection method would be expected to find the given species (confirmed absence), or a species was not looked for (e.g. a trap failure) Preferably, a zero indicates a species was looked for and not found, and a NA represents a species was not looked for/trap failure/ etc. Blank values are highly discouraged Authors might also assert a definition of absence.

raw_full_info.examples: "Zero indicates a species was looked for and not found. NA represents a trap failure"; "When a species is indicated as absent, it was expected due to extensive sampling and found in other places during the study but not found here."

GPS information.name: GPS information
GPS information.descr: If raw GPS data is obfuscated in any way, a statement on the manner by which this occurred should be given. Provide datum/SRS and (if known) GPS unit accuracy; indicate obfuscation method if used.
GPS information.evidence: If raw GPS data is obfuscated in any way, a statement on the manner by which this occurred should be given. The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS), if known, can also be identified. GPS unit accuracy could also be provided. The highest resolution data (e.g. trap-level, specific GPS location) are the most useful. It is hoped that no data obfuscation occurs.

raw_full_info.examples: "Raw GPS points have been provided. GPS unit accuracy +/- 8 m"; "GPS locations have had precision reduced by truncating to 3 decimals"; "Points were dithered by displacing points randomly by X distance"; "WGS84 datum used and data was aggregated to 1 km pixels"

Data usage information.name: Data usage information
Data usage information.descr: The data reuse policy for your data. Provide a Creative Commons license identification (recommended: CC0 or CC BY 4.0) to promote reusability.
Data usage information.evidence: The data reuse policy for your data. Please provide a creative commons license identification. Please provide a creative commons license identification. For data to be F.A.I.R., it must be Reusable. We therefore recommend data be provided as “CC0” or “CC BY 4.0”.

Start Time (for collection).name: Start Time (for collection)
Start Time (for collection).descr: Start time of the data sample collection. Be as specific as practically possible. Any unambiguous format is acceptable; provide time zone if relevant. A 24-hour clock is preferred but must be unambiguous.
Start Time (for collection).evidence: Start time of the data sample collection. e.g. The trap was set… Be as specific as practically possible. Any unambiguous format is acceptable. However, do not use two-digit year abbreviations. If relevant, provide time zone in field or in header; a 24 hour clock is preferred but should be made unambiguous as to which time format is being used.

End Time (for collection).name: End Time (for collection)
End Time (for collection).descr: End time of the data sample collection. If instantaneous (e.g. a tick drag), End Time may equal Start Time.
End Time (for collection).evidence: End time of the data sample collection. e.g. The trap was collected… See above. If instantaneous data collection (e.g. a tick drag), End Time may be the same as Start Time.

raw_full_info.examples: Same formats as Start Time; End Time may equal Start Time for instantaneous collections.

Location.name: Location
Location.descr: Geographical location of sample collection. Provide as detailed as possible, preferably decimalized latitude and longitude with specified accuracy; provide place/trap name as well. If obfuscation was used, indicate in metadata.
Location.evidence: The geographical location of sample collection. As detailed as possible. Latitude and longitude if possible with specified accuracy Providing both a GPS point (decimalized GPS points are preferred) field and a geographical name field is preferred. Note only providing location names is highly discouraged as they change over time and can be ambiguous. Both Place / Trap names and GPS fields can be provided. If obfuscation was used, it should be indicated in the Metadata (Online-only Table 1). Splitting latitude and longitude further into two columns further reduces ambiguity.

raw_full_info.examples: "Kukar Maikiya, Jigawa State, Nigeria" and "40.697" and "-74.015"

Collection method.name: Collection method
Collection method.descr: Sampling apparatus or observation method (e.g. trap type, observation method).
Collection method.evidence: Sampling apparatus (e.g. trap type, observation method) "CDC light trap" "Tick drag" "Quadrat count" "BG Sentinel Trap" "Pitfall trap" "Sticky trap" "Larval dip" "Johnson suction trap" "Lindgren Funnel Trap"

raw_full_info.examples: "CDC light trap"; "BG Sentinel Trap"; "Pitfall trap"; "Tick drag"

Collection attractants.name: Collection attractants
Collection attractants.descr: Attractant or lure used to attract organisms to a trap or collection. Be specific; explicitly state if none was used.
Collection attractants.evidence: The attractant/ lures used to attract insects to a trap or collection Please be as specific as possible. For example, a cow used as bait should be referred to as a ‘cow’ and not ‘animal’, or specify the attractant used, such as ‘CO2’ Company names, in particular for chemical attractants, are helpful. Please explicitly state if no attractant was used.

Collection area.name: Collection area
Collection area.descr: Spatial extent (area or volume) of the sample (e.g. transect/quadrat area or volume). Not typically used for passive fixed traps.
Collection area.evidence: The spatial extent (area or volume) of the sample. If relevant (e.g., when collection method is transect or quadrat), in units of area or volume, the spatial coverage of the sampling unit. Note this field would not typically be used for passive collections from fixed traps.

Taxonomy.name: Taxonomy
Taxonomy.descr: Taxonomic classification of the sample collected; scientific genus and species preferred (avoid abbreviations).
Taxonomy.evidence: Classification of sample collected. Scientific genus and species preferred. Avoid abbreviation.

Unit(s) of measurement and observation.name: Unit(s) of measurement and observation
Unit(s) of measurement and observation.descr: Description of exactly what was observed and the unit for the 'Value' field (e.g. life stage, sex). Units should not be abbreviated; consider separate fields for sex/stage.
Unit(s) of measurement and observation.evidence: Description of exactly what was observed, the unit for the field "Value," below. For counts, should indicate life stage, sex, etc. Unit measures can be encoded into value field header. Consider multiple unit fields (e.g. separate fields for sex and stage.) See Fig. 2. Do not abbreviate. Coded data key should be provided in field name (e.g. "1 = species present 0 = species absent").

raw_full_info.examples: "Number of individuals per m^2"; "Adult Females"; "Males and Females"; "Nymphs"

Value.name: Value
Value.descr: The numerical amount or result from the sample collection (often a count of observed individuals). Units should be provided in a separate field or header.
Value.evidence: The numerical amount or result from the sample collection. Often this will be a quantity of observed individuals. Unit measures can be encoded into value field header. See Fig. 2. Units should be provided in a separate field or in the header.

Additional sample information.name: Additional sample information
Additional sample information.descr: Additional fields to capture experimental variables, sub-locations, host/plant cultivar/species, environmental covariates (e.g. wind, temperature, elevation), or voucher specimen disposition.
Additional sample information.evidence: This could be more than one field and should be used when more information is required to understand the experiment, for example experimental variables, sub-locations, plant host cultivar/species, etc. Some users may report wind speeds, temperatures, elevations etc. This could also include data on disposition of any voucher specimen.

raw_full_info.examples: "Forest" vs "Field"; "Winter" vs "Summer"; "Inside" vs "Outside"; "200 meters above sea level"

Sample Name.name: Sample Name
Sample Name.descr: A human-readable sample name used by the depositor for organization; may be used to tie related observations together.
Sample Name.evidence: A human readable sample name. May exist solely for the benefit of the depositor in organizing their data, use their own internal naming conventions etc. May also be used to tie related observations together. This field may be useful for updating records once deposited in a repository.

SampleID.name: SampleID
SampleID.descr: A unique identifier for the sample/observation (mapping suggested to eventID in Darwin Core).
SampleID.evidence: SampleID eventID Sample Name e.g. fieldNumber for individual observations; see also SampleID above for the field names for the complex samples See Wieczorek et al. 64 for more information.

standards.notes: MIReAD includes explicit mapping tables to GBIF and Darwin Core (see Table 1 and Table 2 in the source). The extracted fields above are taken verbatim from the Online-only Table 1 (Study Information/resource metadata) and Online-only Table 2 (data/sample fields) in the published manuscript.
